intro: The Palestinian territories are two separate areas: the hilly West Bank beside the Jordan River, and the small, flat, crowded Gaza Strip on the Mediterranean.

chapters.title: The West Bank
text: The West Bank is mostly hills covered in olive groves and terraces, falling steeply to the Jordan Valley and the Dead Sea in the east. Jericho, near the Dead Sea, lies about 250 m below sea level.
Israeli settlements, roads and checkpoints divide the land, and the Israeli-built separation barrier runs through and around it.

chapters.title: The Gaza Strip
text: Gaza is about 41 km long and up to 12 km wide, with over two million people, one of the most densely populated places on Earth. It borders Israel and Egypt.

chapters.title: Water and climate
text: Summers are hot and dry. Water is scarce, and much of Gaza's groundwater is too salty to drink.

keyTerms.meaning: An Israeli community built in occupied territory.
